transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-05 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (RDW AE), Jared (RDW SE), Sophie (RDW CSM), Ethan (Arcadia ML lead), Priya (Arcadia Infra), Daniel (Arcadia CTO)

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick agenda — microburst recap, kernel sweep results so far, seqlen telemetry, and next profiling window.
[00:18] Ethan: yep thanks Maya. quick context — last week we saw a couple of spikes in TTFT around the 200 to 300ms p99 which bumped our user-facing latency. traffic's around 420 rps normal, bursts up to 1.2k for a few seconds.
[00:32] Priya: and to add, our infra is 4x A100-ish hosts in a VPC, with shared KV cache. we do off-host logging and the KMS rules are strict — logs only to our bucket.
[00:45] Jared: okay, that pattern fits microburst windowing. a couple of questions first — what's your typical prompt distribution seqlen? is it lots of short prompts or a long tail?
[01:02] Ethan: mostly short, like 8 to 32 tokens for queries, but we have a 5% tail that hits 256 to 512 tokens; that's customer support transcripts.
[01:15] Maya: that's helpful — the tail could be pushing batching/kv warming. we saw in earlier runs that when mixed seqlens are present, the runtime sometimes falls back to a different kernel path which increases latency for first tokens.
[01:34] Daniel: that fallback — can you explain briefly? is it deterministic per request or dynamic?
[01:40] Jared: it's dynamic — the runtime chooses kernels based on sequence-length histogram and current occupancy. if the batch includes long sequences, it might pick kernel variants optimized for long seqlen which are heavier on startup. that can push TTFT for short requests in the batch.
[01:58] Priya: hmm we do see simultaneous small user requests with a few long ones. we don't intentionally route by seqlen yet.
[02:10] Maya: right, so two levers: seqlen-based routing/pinning and kernel hedging. we've been experimenting with hedging where we send an initial small-path kernel for TTFT then let a heavier kernel finish for throughput.
[02:27] Ethan: that sounds promising. any telemetry from your side that shows impact?
[02:32] Jared: yes, on our midweek run we tried a hedging config on a sample workload — p50 stayed the same but p99 improved ~120ms in the burst window. caveat: cost went up ~6% because of duplicated work.
[02:47] Maya: and we believe with smarter caching (prefix/KV warm) the cost overhead drops. but we need to validate on customer traces.
[02:58] Ethan: can you run that hedging on our trace? we can provide samples.
[03:05] Jared: yes — that's on the action items. i'll do a kernel sweep using your sample trace. question — do you want int8/4-bit quant variants included?
[03:15] Priya: yes include both int8 and our 4-bit quantized model variant. we want to understand accuracy/latency tradeoffs.
[03:23] Daniel: on accuracy — we've seen slight probability shifts on edge cases; what do you recommend measuring?
[03:29] Maya: run standard eval prompts we shared last month, plus a small set of failure cases. we'll compare logits and top-k alignment. note: sometimes small quant changes increase first-token time due to different kernel selection.
[03:44] Ethan: okay. on infra — Priya mentioned shared KV cache. can cache thrashing cause these microbursts?
[03:51] Jared: absolutely. if the KV cache is cold for a given set of keys, the runtime pulls from disk/host, which adds 60–120ms. in bursts, many keys shift and cache eviction spikes. we need perf counters to confirm.
[04:06] Priya: we can enable more counters but might need to coordinate a short maintenance window to share access.
[04:12] Maya: Sophie, Sophie — can you coordinate that window with Arcadia?
[04:16] Sophie: yep I'll send a Doodle and propose two 1-hr slots next week.
[04:20] Ethan: perfect.
[04:22] [04:22] Jared: also a quick note on streaming vs buffered responses — when responses are streamed we see earlier first bytes but sometimes more microburst variability because the model's left-to-right pipeline affects scheduling. buffering can smooth but costs latency for first byte.
[04:39] Daniel: so streaming helps TTFT but might make p99 worse in bursts?
[04:44] Jared: in some configs, yes. it's tradeoff. for short prompts streaming usually wins; for mixed seqlen bursts buffering + seqlen routing helps.
[04:55] Ethan: what's Redwood's recommended default for mixed workloads?
[04:58] Maya: default: seqlen-aware routing with a small streaming window for short prompts, fallback to buffered for larger. and kernel hedging enabled at 20% sample rate initially.
[05:11] Priya: can you share the sample rate rationale? why 20%?
[05:15] Jared: 20% gives enough signal to measure p99 impact without doubling cost across the board. once we hit a stable hedging config we scale down samples.
[05:25] Ethan: sounds reasonable.
[05:28] [10:02] Maya: jumping ahead — Jared, any anomalies from last kernel sweep?
[10:06] Jared: yeah one weirdness: for the 4-bit quant run on our A100 profile the kernel fused-matmul path regressed at seqlen ~64; p99 spiked unexpectedly. likely an integer overflow/tiling mismatch in that kernel. we need to run microbench with perf counters on Arcadia nodes to confirm.
[10:25] Priya: that's the sort of thing our infra team can help capture if you tell us what counters to enable.
[10:30] Jared: we'll send a short list — L2 miss rate, memcpy times, NVLINK spikes, and kernel launch latency.
[10:37] Daniel: do you expect code-level fixes quickly or is this a kernel vendor issue?
[10:42] Jared: uncertain — sometimes it's a kernel selection heuristic; other times it's a geometry/tile-size problem we patch in runtime. we should treat it as an unknown until we profile.
[10:51] Ethan: ok allocated priority then.
[10:55] [18:15] Maya: quick commercial question — at what point should we recommend Redwood Dedicated vs hosted for this workload?
[18:21] Jared: if your p99 SLO is strict and you want predictable microburst handling, Dedicated with pinned pools and seqlen routing is better. Hosted can work with hedging but has more variability in noisy neighbor scenarios.
[18:35] Daniel: cost delta?
[18:38] Maya: roughly Dedicated committed capacity will increase base cost but reduces microburst tail risk. we'll send a cost comparison sheet.
[18:45] Ethan: please do.
[18:47] Maya: Sophie — include a committed capacity scenario in the next doc.
[18:50] Sophie: noted.
[18:52] [27:00] Priya: another data point — our observability shows a correlation between background batch jobs (indexing) and the observed bursts. could that be cross-host network saturation?
[27:10] Jared: yes, NVLINK or PCIe congestion during heavy memcpy phases can delay kernel launches. counters will confirm.
[27:20] Ethan: we can try isolating the test hosts from background jobs during profiling.
[27:24] Priya: we'll schedule that for the profiling window.
[27:28] [35:05] Maya: recap — action items: Jared runs kernel sweep on Arcadia traces including int8 and 4-bit; Priya/Ethan provide seqlen distribution + perf counters window; Maya sends benchmark/cost sheet; Sophie schedules profiling slot.
[35:22] Daniel: timeline?
[35:25] Maya: target to have initial sweep + telemetry analysis in this sprint — expecting results by 2027-04-09.
[35:33] Ethan: good.
[35:35] [41:45] Jared: one more technical note — if the KV cache shows high eviction rates during bursts we can try a short-lived prefetch for keys associated with support transcripts. that often cuts 80–120ms.
[41:58] Priya: do you mean a warm-up request or a background prefetch?
[42:03] Jared: background prefetch at the start of a predicted window; or tiny synchronous warm-ups when a user session initialises. needs coordination with your privacy rules.
[42:15] Ethan: privacy flagged — we can't persist keys outside the VPC, but we can prefetch in-memory within the same host.
[42:22] Maya: we can support host-local prefetch via Dedicated or via VPC deployment on Redwood Private. we'll detail options.
[42:34] [48:50] Sophie: next steps recap in calendar invite and i'll attach the benchmark spreadsheet and the list of perf counters.
[48:58] Maya: thanks everyone. any final Qs?
[49:02] Daniel: none from me.
[49:05] Ethan: all good. thanks.
[49:08] Maya: great — we'll follow up with the artifacts and the proposed profiling windows. bye.
[49:12] End of recording.
